net/ip#

IP addresses and networks, IPv4 and IPv6.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let address = IpAddress("192.168.1.10");
address.version();                                  // IpVersion.v4
address.properties().membership(IpProperty.private_network);   // true
let network = IpNetwork(IpAddress("10.0.0.0"), 8);
network.membership(IpAddress("10.1.2.3"));           // true
for IpAddresses(IpNetwork(IpAddress("192.168.0.0"), 30)) -> each { … }

Description#

IP addresses and networks, IPv4 and IPv6.

Properties come from the IANA special-purpose registries.

object IpNetwork#

object IpNetwork

Inclusive CIDR interval. Host bits are masked at construction; the original IpAddress stays unchanged. broadcast() means the final address for both IP versions, not an IPv6 broadcast transport. membership includes both ends. size() uses int even for IPv4 and is exact for the entire IPv6 /0 space. Every observation uses at most 16 octets; no address list is materialized.

object IpInterface#

object IpInterface

Host address plus validated prefix, without OS interface ownership or lookup. address() preserves host bits; network() observes their normalized CIDR range. string() is canonical host/prefix (unbracketed IPv6, without a port or zone).

object IpAddresses#

object IpAddresses does Iterating<IpAddress>

Lazy inclusive traversal of a CIDR network, including network/final addresses. cursor() is independent and immutable; successor() never changes its receiver. Only the current and final address are retained, even for IPv6 /0. Apply Taken or use the cursor before materializing a bounded prefix of a huge interval.
